fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is defeated by G13/G15. A fixed coefficient-sum-one affine collision passes through every linear bag marginal, and because bag cells partition the fixed coefficients, each bag has squared energy at most the squared l1 norm of those coefficients—an instance-independent constant, directly meeting the proposal's falsification condition.

Proposal 2's stated universal one-coordinate clipping property forces the Gram matrix to be diagonal: for clipping z_i=2 to 1, any nonzero Q_ij lets an unrestricted z_j make the objective change have either sign. A diagonal quadratic objective is separable and cannot encode OR or clause consistency, so the proposed M-matrix search cannot realize its mechanism.

Proposal 3 has an explicit entangled shortcut. For any base signed state s with sum one and squared norm q, the tensor-square coefficient matrix diag(s) has both one-factor marginals equal to s, outer normalization one, and squared norm q rather than q^2.

Proposal 4 has no amplification law: tensor powers of the finite S3 standard representation acquire invariant tensors already in the square, and finite-group eigenangles do not grow with representation depth. A base-instance holonomy pass therefore cannot imply G20/G21 polynomial relative growth, while affine and signed invariant sections remain unaudited.

Proposal 5 proves at most growth of homogeneous kernel representatives under a formal Lawrence matrix. No fixed CVP target or layer-selection construction shows that every satisfying assignment pays only one layer while all harmful affine fibers must occupy paired layers; absent that, layer count and completeness cost can grow with the harmful norm and leave the relative gap constant.

Proposal 6 still fails the prior reopening condition. The glue topology, target representatives, finite state equivalence, DROP/malformed classes, baseline, contracted legal and illegal costs, and recursive closure inequality are not statically defined; truncating at B+16 can omit high-cost boundary states that cancel and re-enter cheaply later.
evidence: G13 verifies a harmful integral affine combination of globally consistent encodings with coefficients summing to one. G15 carries exactly that combination through every tested hierarchy node with zero residual below threshold.

G19 verifies that unrestricted integral coefficients create an exact accepting signed flow with two negative entries and zero residual. Any transfer, holonomy, or lifting proposal must include such signed and affine fibers rather than infer nonnegative decomposition.

G7, G9, and G11 exhibit exact zero-residual signed or parity states of constant anchor excess; G12 shows that charging parity exposes a cheaper clause drop. Residual amplification alone is therefore insufficient.
G14 supplies only a finite pair-bag shell pass through B+32. It provides no recursive closure or polynomial relative-gap theorem that Proposal 1 or 6 may inherit.
No proposal supplies new verifier output. Proposals 2 and 3 are analytically blocked, while the proposed experiments for 4–6 omit data needed to define a complete unrestricted CVP search.
